title: Go Tutorial
description: Learn Go (Golang) step-by-step, from installation to working with structs and concurrency. Includes interactive code challenges and practical examples for each topic.

content.content: Install Go
Go can be installed from the official website: https://go.dev/dl/

content: Download and install Go for your OS
Add Go to your PATH (usually done automatically)

content.content: Hello World Program
Go programs start with a package declaration and a `main` function.

questions.question: Write a Go program to print 'Hello, Go!'

content.content: Comments in Go
Go supports single-line `//` and multi-line `/* ... */` comments.

questions.question: Write a comment saying 'My first Go program' and print Hello

content.content: Declaring Variables
Variables in Go are declared using the `var` keyword, or with shorthand `:=`.

var x int = 5
y := "John"
fmt.Println(x)
fmt.Println(y)

questions.question: Create a variable age with value 25 and print it

content.content: Data Types in Go
Go has types such as int, float32, float64, string, bool, array, slice, map, and struct.

var a int = 10
var b float64 = 3.14
var c string = "Hello"

questions.question: Create int, float, and string variables and print each

content.content: Working with Numbers
Go supports integers, floats, and complex numbers.

var x int = 1
var y float64 = 2.5
z := complex(3, 4)
fmt.Println(z)

questions.question: Assign a complex number 2+3i to a variable and print it

content.content: Type Conversion
Go requires explicit type conversion between different types.

questions.question: Convert integer 42 to float and print it

content.content: Working with Strings
Strings in Go are UTF-8 encoded and support slicing.

str := "Golang"
fmt.Println(str[0])        // ASCII code
fmt.Println(str[0:4])     // Substring

questions.question: Store 'Golang' in a variable and print the first 4 letters

content.content: Boolean Values
Booleans in Go can be true or false and are used in conditions.

fmt.Println(10 > 9)
fmt.Println(10 == 9)

questions.question: Write an expression that returns true if 7 is greater than 3

content.content: Operators in Go
Go supports arithmetic, comparison, logical, and assignment operators.

a := 5
b := 3
fmt.Println(a + b)
fmt.Println(a * b)
Arrays
Arrays in Go have a fixed size and contain elements of the same type.

var arr = [3]int{1, 2, 3}
fmt.Println(arr[1])

questions.question: Create an array of 3 numbers and print the second number

content.content: Slices
Slices are more powerful than arrays and allow dynamic resizing.

nums := []int{1, 2, 3, 4}
fmt.Println(nums[1:3])

questions.question: Create a slice of 4 numbers and print the last two

content.content: Maps
Maps are key-value stores in Go.

m := map[string]int{"age": 30, "year": 2025}
fmt.Println(m["age"])

questions.question: Create a map with name and age, print name

content.content: If...Else Statements
Go supports if, else if, and else blocks.

questions.question: Write an if statement that prints 'Yes' if 5 is less than 10

content.content: Switch Statement
Go's switch is concise and powerful, without fallthrough by default.

x := 2
switch x {
case 1:
    fmt.Println("One")
case 2:
    fmt.Println("Two")
}

questions.question: Write a switch statement that prints 'Three' if variable is 3
